title: HTML Was Created by Tim Berners-Lee in 1990
fact: Tim Berners-Lee invented HTML (HyperText Markup Language) in 1990 as part of the World Wide Web project at CERN.

title: Forests Help Combat Climate Change
fact: Forests absorb about 2.6 billion tons of CO2 annually, helping to mitigate climate change. Protecting forests is crucial for meeting climate goals.

title: The Crusades Occurred 1095-1291
fact: The Crusades were a series of religious wars between Christians and Muslims over control of holy sites. There were at least nine major Crusades.

title: Giraffes Only Sleep 2 Hours Per Day
fact: Giraffes sleep an average of 1.9 hours per day, often in short naps lasting just a few minutes. This helps them stay alert for predators.

title: The Hubble Space Telescope Orbits Earth Every 95 Minutes
fact: The Hubble Space Telescope orbits Earth at about 340 miles altitude, completing one orbit every 95 minutes. It has observed galaxies 13.4 billion light-years away.

title: Your Hair Grows 6 Inches Per Year
fact: Hair grows about 0.5 mm per day, or 6 inches per year. Scalp hair grows faster than body hair, and growth is faster in summer than winter.

title: The Nile Is the Longest River at 4,132 Miles
fact: The Nile River is approximately 4,132 miles long, making it the longest river in the world. It flows through 11 countries in northeastern Africa.

title: Cows Can Remember 50 Other Cows
fact: Cows have excellent memories and can recognize at least 50 other cows in their herd. They also form close friendships with specific individuals.

title: The First Operating System Was Created in 1964
fact: The first operating system, CTSS (Compatible Time-Sharing System), was developed at MIT in 1964, allowing multiple users to access a computer simultaneously.

title: Trees Can Absorb 48 Pounds of CO2 Per Year
fact: A single tree can absorb about 48 pounds of carbon dioxide per year and release enough oxygen for two people to breathe.

title: The Treaty of Versailles Was Signed in 1919
fact: The Treaty of Versailles officially ended World War I in 1919. It imposed heavy penalties on Germany, which later contributed to World War II.

title: Starfish Can Regenerate Lost Arms
fact: Starfish can regenerate lost arms, and some species can regrow an entire body from a single arm. Some species can have up to 40 arms.

title: The Moon Orbits Earth Every 27.3 Days
fact: The Moon takes 27.3 days to orbit Earth, but the lunar cycle (new moon to new moon) is 29.5 days due to Earth's movement around the Sun.

title: Your Brain Contains 86 Billion Neurons
fact: The human brain contains about 86 billion neurons, each connected to thousands of others via synapses, creating a network of about 100 trillion connections.

title: Antarctica Contains 70% of Earth's Freshwater
fact: Antarctica contains about 70% of Earth's fresh water, stored as ice. If all this ice melted, global sea levels would rise about 200 feet.

title: Sharks Have Been on Earth for 450 Million Years
fact: Sharks have existed for 450 million years, predating dinosaurs by 200 million years. They survived all five mass extinctions.

title: The First Smartphone Was the IBM Simon in 1994
fact: The IBM Simon Personal Communicator, released in 1994, is considered the first smartphone. It had a touchscreen, email, and could send faxes.

title: Forests Provide Habitat for 80% of Land Species
fact: Forests are home to about 80% of terrestrial biodiversity, including 80% of amphibians, 75% of birds, and 65% of mammals.

title: The Black Death Occurred 1346-1353
fact: The Black Death killed an estimated 75-200 million people in Eurasia, wiping out 30-60% of Europe's population in just a few years.

title: Crocodiles Can Hold Their Breath for Over an Hour
fact: Crocodiles can hold their breath for over an hour underwater. They slow their heart rate to conserve oxygen during dives.

title: Your Heart Beats 100,000 Times Per Day
fact: Your heart beats about 100,000 times per day, pumping about 2,000 gallons of blood. Over a lifetime, it beats more than 2.5 billion times.

title: The Sahara Desert Is 3.6 Million Square Miles
fact: The Sahara is the largest hot desert in the world at 3.6 million square miles. However, Antarctica is larger overall if all deserts are considered.

title: Bees Communicate Through Dance
fact: Bees use the waggle dance to communicate the location of food sources to other bees. The dance angle indicates direction relative to the Sun.

title: The First Computer Mouse Was Made of Wood
fact: The first computer mouse, invented in 1964 by Doug Engelbart, was made of wood with two perpendicular wheels that tracked movement.

title: Forests Store Carbon for Thousands of Years
fact: Forests store carbon in their biomass and soil for hundreds to thousands of years. Old-growth forests can store more carbon than younger ones.

title: The Magna Carta Was Signed in 1215
fact: The Magna Carta was signed by King John of England in 1215, establishing that everyone, including the king, was subject to the law.

title: A Cockroach Can Live Without Its Head
fact: A cockroach can survive for weeks without its head because its brain is not in its head. It breathes through spiracles along its body.

title: The Sun Makes Up 99.86% of Solar System Mass
fact: The Sun contains 99.86% of all mass in the solar system. Jupiter alone accounts for most of the remaining mass.

title: Your Skin Has 3 Layers
fact: Human skin has three main layers: epidermis (outer), dermis (middle), and hypodermis (inner). Together, they form the body's largest organ.

title: Lake Victoria Is Africa's Largest Lake
fact: Lake Victoria is the largest lake in Africa and the second largest freshwater lake in the world, covering 68,800 square kilometers.

title: Parrots Can Live to Be Over 80 Years Old
fact: Large parrots like macaws and cockatoos can live 60-80+ years. Some African grey parrots have been documented living over 60 years in captivity.

title: JavaScript Was Created in 10 Days
fact: Brendan Eich created JavaScript in just 10 days in 1995, originally called LiveScript. It became one of the most widely used programming languages.

title: Forests Help Prevent Floods
fact: Forests absorb rainfall and slow runoff, reducing flood risks. Tree roots absorb water and release it slowly, maintaining stream flows.

title: The French Revolution Started in 1789
fact: The French Revolution began on July 14, 1789, with the storming of the Bastille. It transformed France from a monarchy to a republic.

title: Elephants Are the Only Animals That Can't Jump
fact: Adult elephants are the only land mammals that cannot jump. Despite this, they can run up to 25 mph and swim excellently.

title: The Longest Daylight Period Is 24 Hours at the Poles
fact: At the poles, the Sun doesn't set for about 6 months during summer. This creates periods of 24-hour daylight alternating with 24-hour darkness.

title: Your Blood Vessels Would Circle Earth Twice
fact: If all blood vessels were laid end to end, they would stretch about 60,000 miles—enough to circle the Earth more than twice.

title: Mount Everest Is 29,029 Feet Tall
fact: Mount Everest stands at 29,029 feet (8,848 meters) above sea level, making it the tallest mountain on Earth. It grows about 4mm taller each year.

title: Dolphins Sleep With One Eye Open
fact: Dolphins practice unihemispheric sleep, keeping one eye open and half their brain awake to watch for predators and remember to breathe.

title: WiFi Signals Travel at the Speed of Light
fact: WiFi signals travel at the speed of light (about 300,000 km/s), but interference and obstacles can slow them down.

title: Trees Can Reduce Air Pollution
fact: Trees absorb pollutants like ozone, nitrogen dioxide, and sulfur dioxide through their leaves. A single tree can remove 0.4-1.5 pounds of pollutants annually.

title: The Library of Alexandria Burned in 48 BCE
fact: The Library of Alexandria, the ancient world's greatest repository of knowledge, was partially destroyed by fire during Julius Caesar's siege of Alexandria.

title: Tardigrades Survive in Space
fact: Tardigrades (water bears) are the only animals that can survive in outer space. They can withstand extreme radiation, temperatures, and vacuum.

title: The Moon Is 4.5 Billion Years Old
fact: The Moon formed about 4.5 billion years ago, shortly after Earth. It likely formed when a Mars-sized body collided with early Earth.

title: Your Brain Uses 20% of Body Energy
fact: Despite being only 2% of body weight, the brain uses 20% of the body's energy and oxygen. This makes it extremely sensitive to deprivation.

title: The Great Barrier Reef Has 1,500 Fish Species
fact: The Great Barrier Reef is home to about 1,500 species of fish, 4,000 types of mollusks, and 400 species of coral.

title: Honey Never Spoils
fact: Archaeologists have found 3,000-year-old honey in Egyptian tombs that was still edible. Honey's low moisture and acidic pH prevent bacterial growth.

title: The First Camera Took 8 Hours to Expose an Image
fact: The first photograph (1826-1827) by Nicéphore Niépce took about 8 hours to expose. Modern cameras capture images in fractions of a second.

title: Trees Can Absorb 100 Gallons of Water Daily
fact: A large tree can absorb and transpire up to 100 gallons of water from the soil daily, helping regulate local humidity and rainfall patterns.

title: The Pyramids of Giza Were Built Around 2560 BCE
fact: The Great Pyramid of Giza was built around 2560 BCE for Pharaoh Khufu. It was the tallest structure in the world for over 3,800 years.

title: Owls Can Turn Their Heads 270 Degrees
fact: Owls have 14 neck vertebrae (humans have 7) and can rotate their heads up to 270 degrees. This compensates for their fixed eyeballs.

title: The Universe Is 13.8 Billion Years Old
fact: The universe began with the Big Bang about 13.8 billion years ago. The first stars formed about 200 million years after this event.

title: Your Nose Can Remember 50,000 Scents
fact: Humans can distinguish about 1 trillion different odors, though we only have about 400 types of smell receptors. Memory of scents is stored long-term.

title: The Amazon Contains 20% of World Rivers
fact: The Amazon River system carries more water than any other river system, discharging about 7.2 million cubic feet per second into the Atlantic.

title: Sharks Can Detect Electrical Fields
fact: Sharks can detect electrical fields as small as a billionth of a volt using special organs called ampullae of Lorenzini. This helps them find prey.

title: Python Was Named After Monty Python
fact: Guido van Rossum named Python after the British comedy troupe Monty Python, not the snake. He was reading Monty Python scripts when developing the language.

title: Forests Provide 75% of Urban Freshwater
fact: About 75% of accessible freshwater for urban areas comes from forested watersheds. Forests filter and regulate water flow throughout the year.

title: The Industrial Revolution Started in Britain in 1760
fact: The Industrial Revolution began in Britain around 1760, transforming economies from agricultural to industrial. It spread to Europe and America by the 1800s.

title: Crows Recognize Human Faces
fact: Crows can recognize and remember human faces for years. They can teach other crows which people are dangerous, passing this knowledge through generations.

title: The Largest Galaxy Has 100 Trillion Stars
fact: IC 1101 is the largest known galaxy, containing about 100 trillion stars and stretching 6 million light-years across.

title: Your Small Intestine Has a Surface Area of 2,700 sq ft
fact: If unfolded, the small intestine's surface area would cover about 2,700 square feet—roughly the size of a tennis court.

title: The Mariana Trench Is 36,070 Feet Deep
fact: The Mariana Trench reaches 36,070 feet (10,994 meters) at its deepest point, called the Challenger Deep. Pressure there is 1,000 times atmospheric pressure.

title: Flamingos Are Born Grey, Not Pink
fact: Flamingos are born with grey/white feathers. They turn pink from eating shrimp and blue-green algae that contain carotenoid pigments.

title: The First Email Was Sent in 1971
fact: Ray Tomlinson sent the first network email in 1971, using the @ sign to separate usernames from computer names on ARPANET.

title: Forests Are Home to 1.6 Billion People
fact: About 1.6 billion people globally depend on forests for their livelihoods, including food, medicine, fuel, and income.

title: The First Human Spaceflight Was in 1961
fact: Soviet cosmonaut Yuri Gagarin became the first human in space on April 12, 1961, completing one orbit of Earth in 108 minutes.

title: Sloths Are Excellent Swimmers
fact: Despite being slow on land, sloths can swim three times faster using a breaststroke technique. They can hold their breath for 40 minutes.

title: The Nearest Galaxy to Milky Way Is 25,000 Light-Years Away
fact: The Canis Major Dwarf Galaxy, at 25,000 light-years away, is the nearest galaxy to the Milky Way, though it's being absorbed by our galaxy.

title: Your Body Has 37.2 Trillion Cells
fact: The human body contains approximately 37.2 trillion cells, with red blood cells making up about 70% of all cells in the body.

title: Canada Has 60% of World's Lakes
fact: Canada has about 60% of all the lakes in the world, with over 2 million lakes covering about 9% of its territory.

title: Dragonflies Have 30,000 Eyes
fact: Dragonflies have compound eyes with about 30,000 facets, giving them nearly 360-degree vision. They can see ultraviolet light.

title: WiFi Was Invented in Australia in the 1990s
fact: WiFi technology was developed by CSIRO in Australia in the 1990s. The term 'WiFi' doesn't actually stand for anything—it's a trademarked brand name.

title: Forests Can Take 100 Years to Recover
fact: After clear-cutting, a forest can take 100-200 years to fully recover its biodiversity and ecological functions. Some species require centuries to return.

title: The World Wide Web Was Invented in 1989
fact: Tim Berners-Lee invented the World Wide Web in 1989 at CERN, combining hypertext with the internet to create a global information space.

title: A Whale's Throat Is Only 4 Inches Wide
fact: A blue whale, the largest animal ever, has a throat only about 4 inches wide. It eats mainly tiny krill, not large fish or people.

title: Venus Spins Backwards Compared to Other Planets
fact: Venus rotates clockwise (retrograde rotation) while most other planets rotate counterclockwise. A day on Venus is longer than its year.

title: Your Brain Is 73% Water
fact: The brain is 73% water, and even 2% dehydration can impair cognitive function, mood, and concentration.

title: The Amazon Rainforest Has 15% of World Biodiversity
fact: The Amazon contains about 10% of all species on Earth, despite covering less than 1% of Earth's surface. Many species remain undiscovered.

title: Wombats Produce Cube-Shaped Poop
fact: Wombats produce cube-shaped feces to prevent rolling away and mark territory more effectively. They can produce up to 100 cubes per night.

title: USB Standards Have Evolved Since 1996
fact: USB 1.0 (1996) transferred at 12 Mbps, USB 2.0 (2000) at 480 Mbps, USB 3.0 (2008) at 5 Gbps, and USB 4.0 (2019) at 40 Gbps.

title: Trees Can Absorb Sound and Create Quiet Spaces
fact: A 100-foot-wide belt of trees can reduce noise by 50%, absorbing and blocking sound waves. This is why forests feel so peaceful.

title: The First GPS Satellite Was Launched in 1978
fact: The first GPS satellite was launched in 1978. The full GPS constellation of 24 satellites became operational in 1995.

title: Frogs Don't Drink Through Their Mouth
fact: Frogs absorb water through a 'drinking patch' on their belly called the ventral skin. They also breathe and absorb moisture through their skin.

title: The Sun Contains 99.86% of Solar System Mass
fact: The Sun accounts for 99.86% of all mass in the solar system. Its gravity holds all planets, moons, and asteroids in orbit.

title: Your Lungs Have 300 Million Alveoli
fact: Your lungs contain about 300 million tiny air sacs (alveoli). If spread flat, they would cover about 70 square meters.

title: Iceland Has No Mosquitoes
fact: Iceland is one of few countries with no native mosquito species, likely due to its harsh, variable climate that prevents larvae from surviving.

title: Pandas Spend 12 Hours a Day Eating
fact: Giant pandas spend 10-16 hours per day eating bamboo because it is low in nutrients and hard to digest. They consume 26-84 pounds daily.

title: The First Smartphone Virus Appeared in 2004
fact: Cabir was the first smartphone virus, appearing in 2004. It infected Symbian phones via Bluetooth and displayed 'Caribe' on infected devices.

title: Forests Generate 50% of Earth's Oxygen
fact: Forests and oceans together produce about 50% of Earth's oxygen through photosynthesis. Forests alone contribute significantly to this total.

title: The Berlin Wall Was Built in 1961
fact: The Berlin Wall was erected by East Germany on August 13, 1961, dividing East and West Berlin until its fall in 1989.

title: Seahorses Are Monogamous
fact: Seahorses mate for life and perform daily 'dances' to reinforce their bond. The male carries and births the offspring in a specialized pouch.

title: The Moon Has Quakes That Last 10 Minutes
fact: The Moon experiences moonquakes that can last up to 10 minutes, much longer than earthquakes. Some are caused by Earth's gravitational pull.

title: Your Hair Grows 0.5mm Per Day
fact: Hair grows about 0.3-0.5 mm per day, roughly 6 inches per year. Growth is faster in summer than winter and during sleep.

title: The Volga River Is Europe's Longest at 3,530 km
fact: The Volga River in Russia is Europe's longest river at 3,530 km. It flows into the Caspian Sea and drains about one-third of European Russia.

title: Camels Have Three Eyelids
fact: Camels have three eyelids: two with lashes and one transparent one that protects the eye while allowing visibility during sandstorms.

title: The First Computer Mouse Was Invented in 1964
fact: Douglas Engelbart invented the computer mouse in 1964 at Stanford Research Institute. It was made of wood with two perpendicular wheels.

title: Trees Can Detect Forest Fires Early
fact: Trees can detect smoke and chemical signals from damaged neighboring trees, triggering their own defense mechanisms before flames arrive.

title: The American Revolution Occurred 1775-1783
fact: The American Revolutionary War lasted from 1775 to 1783, resulting in American independence from Great Britain.

title: A Cockroach Can Live Weeks Without Its Head
fact: A cockroach can survive for weeks without its head because its brain is not in its head and it breathes through spiracles on its body.
